name: Turborepo Remote Cache
about: Stores Turborepo build artifacts for reuse across developer machines and CI jobs.

variables.label: Cache folder
variables.description: Host folder for cached artifacts, must be writable by UID 1001.

variables.label: Access token
variables.description: Every machine using this cache sends this token. Copy it before you deploy and set it as TURBO_TOKEN wherever you run turbo.

variables.label: Host port
variables.description: Host port used in the TURBO_API URL.

variables.label: Artifact signing key
variables.description: Shared artifact signing key, must also be configured in Turborepo clients with signing enabled.

variables.label: Largest artifact
variables.description: Maximum accepted upload size in bytes.

variables.label: Read-only
variables.description: Serves cached artifacts but rejects uploads and cleanup requests.

variables.label: Log status checks
variables.description: Logs requests to the status endpoint.

variables.label: Authentication
variables.description: Static checks the access token, JWT checks signed tokens, and None permits unauthenticated access.

variables.label: JWKS URL
variables.description: JWKS metadata URL for retrieving the public keys used to verify JWTs.

variables.label: JWT issuer
variables.description: Matched against the iss field in the JWT. Optional even when using JWT authentication.

variables.label: JWT audience
variables.description: Matched against the aud field in the JWT. Optional even when using JWT authentication.

variables.label: Read scopes
variables.description: If set, one of the scopes listed here must be present to read from the cache. Separate several with commas.

variables.label: Write scopes
variables.description: If set, one of the scopes listed here must be present to write to the cache. Separate several with commas.

variables.label: HTTP/2
variables.description: Switch the server to the HTTP/2 protocol. Plain connections lose HTTP/1.1 support, which breaks turbo talking to the cache directly. Leave off unless a proxy in front speaks HTTP/2.

variables.label: Certificates folder
variables.description: Host folder holding the TLS key and certificate, mounted read-only at /certs. Leave blank to serve plain HTTP. Deploy fails if the folder does not exist.

variables.label: TLS key path
variables.description: Where the private key sits inside the container, so under /certs. HTTPS only turns on when this and the certificate path both point at files that exist.

variables.label: TLS certificate path
variables.description: Where the certificate sits inside the container. If either file is missing the server quietly starts on plain HTTP.
